column1: # tests/doom-core/fixtures/source/copy.tsv — what the boundary copy carries.
# One step-written buffer per line that a PORTED CORE reader needs, copied into
# the port's storage once per frame between the tickers and the render. The
# list is checked by tests/doom-core/copy-check.rb in BOTH directions: every
# buffer a ported reader needs is here, and nothing is here that no ported
# reader needs. A buffer enters in the same commit as its first CORE reader, so
# porting a definition that reads step state fails the check until the buffer
# is added, and the list maintains itself rather than being remembered.
# THE SECOND COLUMN IS WHERE LEAVING THE BUFFER OUT FIRST SHOWS in DEMO1: the
# earliest frame at which a live comparison (frame, plane or end-of-frame screen)
# disagrees when SOURCE_PORT_COPY_SKIP names it. tests/doom-core/screens.sh
# asserts that frame EXACTLY, so a poison that equals the truth for a while and
# shows late -- as hud_message_on once did -- fails, and so does one that shows
# somewhere else. The status bar reads its three from frame 0; the first flat
# animates at frame 8; the first HUD message comes on at frame 60; the sprite
# projection and the per-sector walk read the things, their links and the
# sectors from frame 0, and each skipped copy first shows as a leaf
# disagreement there.
# THE THIRD COLUMN, WHERE THERE IS ONE, IS THE BOUND THE COPY RUNS TO. The
# things are copied up to the tick's high-water mark, Game@@mobj_alloc, not to
# their declared capacity limit:maxmobjs (4096): measured over the whole of the
# three demos the mark reaches 222 (DEMO1), 316 (DEMO2) and 273 (DEMO3), so the
# seven arrays cost at most 7 * 316 cells a frame where the capacity would be
# 7 * 4096. The things' links, game_thing_next, are per thing and run to the
# same mark on a row of their own; the sectors' list heads and lights are per
# sector and are copied whole, bounded by the level's declared count. screens.sh
# asserts that no demo passes the mobj_alloc bound, that every row writing one
# writes the same, and that the highest mark reached equals it.
